title: IP address conflict
symptom: Windows warns of an IP address conflict and the network is unreliable
user_description: A message says there's an IP address conflict with another system on the network, and my connection keeps dropping.

options.text: Choose any static address you like and hope it is free
options.why: Guessing can create another conflict. Addresses must come from the DHCP range or a managed list.

options.text: Turn off every other device in the office
options.why: Hugely disruptive and finds nothing out. Look for the specific duplicate.

options.text: Renew the PC's address from DHCP, then find the other device and check whether either has a manually set address overlapping the DHCP range
options.why: Two devices with the same address cause drops. Renewing gives the PC a fresh address, and finding the other device shows the real cause, often a static address inside the DHCP range.
Drastic and unrelated to a duplicate address.

hints: What does it mean when two devices share one address?
How does a PC normally get an address?
What can cause two devices to end up with the same one?
real_world_tip: Keep a record of static addresses. Most conflicts happen because someone set a fixed address without checking.
